claims.text: Flu vaccine side effects are generally mild and go away on their own within a few days (takeaways, tables, duration, FAQ)
claims.quote: Side effects of the flu vaccine are generally mild and go away on their own within a few days.

claims.text: Headache, fever, nausea and muscle aches are common flu shot side effects (common table, FAQ)
claims.quote: Common side effects from the flu shot include: Soreness, redness, and/or swelling from the shot; Headache; Fever; Nausea; Muscle aches

claims.text: Life-threatening allergic reactions are rare; serious side effects rare
claims.quote: Life threatening allergic reactions to the flu shot are rare.

claims.text: Severe allergic reaction signs: difficulty breathing, hoarseness or wheezing, swelling around eyes or lips, hives, paleness, weakness, fast heartbeat or dizziness
claims.quote: Difficulty breathing; Hoarseness or wheezing; Swelling around the eyes or lips; Hives; Paleness; Weakness; A fast heart beat or dizziness

claims.text: Allergic reaction signs most likely within a few minutes to a few hours after the shot
claims.quote: These signs would most likely happen within a few minutes to a few hours after the vaccine is given.

claims.text: Call 911 for a severe allergic reaction or other emergency; otherwise call your doctor
claims.quote: If you think it is a severe allergic reaction or other emergency that can't wait, call 9-1-1 ... Otherwise, call your doctor.

claims.text: Watch for unusual conditions such as a high fever or behavior changes and call your doctor
claims.quote: With any vaccine, look for any unusual conditions, such as a high fever, behavior changes

claims.text: Report the reaction to VAERS
claims.quote: Afterward, the reaction should be reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS).

claims.text: GBS after flu illness, though rare, is more common than after flu vaccination
claims.quote: Even though GBS following flu illness is rare, GBS is more common following flu illness than following flu vaccination.

claims.text: GBS has not been associated with the nasal spray vaccine
claims.quote: GBS has not been associated with the nasal spray vaccine.

claims.text: Side effects not going away after a few days, or soreness that is unusual or not improving, warrant a call to your doctor (inference from 'within a few days' plus 'call your doctor')
claims.quote: Side effects of the flu vaccine are generally mild and go away on their own within a few days.

references.cited_as: CDC. Guillain-Barré Syndrome and Flu Vaccine. Last reviewed September 17, 2024.

claims.text: GBS definition: immune system damages nerve cells, causing muscle weakness and sometimes paralysis
claims.quote: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is a rare disorder in which a person's own immune system damages their nerve cells

claims.text: GBS occurs in about 1 to 2 per 100,000 people in the US each year (shown as 10 to 20 per million, a unit conversion); most cases not associated with vaccines
claims.quote: GBS occurs in about 1 to 2 out of every 100,000 people in the United States each year. Most cases are not associated with vaccines.

claims.text: Data on GBS and seasonal flu vaccination vary across seasons
claims.quote: The data on the association between GBS and seasonal flu vaccination are varied and inconsistent across flu seasons.

claims.text: Any increased GBS risk after flu vaccination is small, on the order of one to two additional cases per million doses (body, chart, FAQ, citable summary)
claims.quote: If there is an increased risk of GBS following flu vaccination, it is small, on the order of one to two additional GBS cases per million doses of flu vaccine administered.

references.cited_as: CDC. Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) and Vaccines. Last reviewed July 31, 2024.

claims.text: Studies suggest a person is more likely to get GBS after getting the flu than after vaccination
claims.quote: Results of these studies suggest that it is more likely that a person will get GBS after getting the flu than after vaccination.

references.cited_as: CDC. Flu Vaccines and People with Egg Allergies. Last reviewed September 17, 2024.

claims.text: People with egg allergy may receive any flu vaccine, egg-based or not, appropriate for age and health
claims.quote: People with egg allergy may receive any flu vaccine (egg-based or non-egg-based) that is otherwise appropriate for their age and health status.

claims.text: Beginning with 2023-2024 season, additional safety measures no longer recommended for egg allergy
claims.quote: Beginning with the 2023-2024 season, additional safety measures are no longer recommended

claims.text: After a severe allergic reaction to a flu vaccine, some people may still get a different flu vaccine depending on which one caused it
claims.quote: People who have had a severe allergic reaction to a flu vaccine in the past should generally not receive flu vaccine again ... might be able to get certain flu vaccines, depending on which one caused the allergic reaction.

claims.text: Flu shot cannot cause flu; made with inactivated (killed) virus or a single protein
claims.quote: Flu vaccines cannot cause flu illness. Flu vaccines given with a needle (i.e., flu shots) are made with either inactivated (killed) viruses, or with only a single protein from an influenza virus.

claims.text: Nasal spray contains live viruses weakened so they will not cause illness
claims.quote: The nasal spray vaccine contains live viruses that are attenuated (weakened) so that they will not cause illness.

claims.text: Most common side effect is soreness, redness, tenderness or swelling where the shot was given
claims.quote: The most common side effects from flu shots are soreness, redness, tenderness or swelling where the shot was given.

claims.text: Injection-site reactions usually begin soon after vaccination and last 1 to 2 days
claims.quote: If these reactions occur, they usually begin soon after vaccination and last 1-2 days.

claims.text: Low-grade fever, headache and muscle aches may occur
claims.quote: Low-grade fever, headache and muscle aches also may occur.

claims.text: Feeling sick may be another respiratory virus, or flu exposure shortly before vaccination or during the two weeks it takes to build protection
claims.quote: Someone can get sick with another respiratory virus besides influenza virus ... Someone can be exposed to influenza viruses shortly before getting vaccinated or during the two-week period after vaccination that it takes the body to develop immune protection.

claims.text: GBS occurs rarely after influenza vaccination; serious reactions rare
claims.quote: a serious neurological condition that can cause paralysis occurs rarely following influenza vaccination

claims.text: Fever, malaise, myalgia and other systemic symptoms can occur; more common in those with no previous exposure (young children), generally less common in adults
claims.quote: Fever, malaise, myalgia, and other systemic symptoms can also occur after inactivated influenza vaccination. These reactions are more common among individuals who have had no previous exposure to the influenza virus antigens

claims.quote: People who have experienced a severe or life threatening allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to a prior dose of any influenza vaccine ... should not receive that vaccine or other vaccines containing that component.

claims.text: Nasal spray weakened live virus cannot cause flu illness

claims.text: Minor flu shot side effects include soreness/redness/swelling, headache, fever, muscle aches, nausea, fatigue
claims.quote: Some minor side effects that may occur are: Soreness, redness, and/or swelling where the shot was given; Headache; Fever; Muscle aches; Nausea; Fatigue

claims.text: Side effects usually mild and short-lasting compared with flu symptoms
claims.quote: These side effects are usually mild and short-lasting, especially when compared to symptoms of flu.

claims.text: Antibodies develop about two weeks after vaccination and protect against influenza infection
claims.quote: It takes about two weeks after vaccination for antibodies to develop in the body and provide protection against influenza virus infection.

claims.text: You cannot get flu from a flu shot because the viruses are killed
claims.quote: The viruses in a flu shot are killed (inactivated), so you cannot get flu from a flu shot.
